channel.title: AI Threat Watch: AI phishing
channel.description: Verified case files in the category AI phishing.

item.title: [MEDIUM] ClaudeFix: shared Claude chats used to deliver ClickFix malware instructions
item.description: Zscaler ThreatLabz describes ClaudeFix, which combines shared Claude chats with the ClickFix paste-and-run technique to deploy malware. Target: Users of shared Claude chat links. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] UAT-11985 uses AI-assisted event lures for Google AitM phishing in Taiwan
item.description: Cisco Talos identified an APT spear-phishing campaign using AI-assisted lures and real-time Google adversary-in-the-middle phishing against Taiwan research affiliates. Target: Individuals at Taiwan research organizations. TW. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] ChatGPT feature abuse paired with ClickFix delivers trojan to users searching via Google
item.description: Huntress found a campaign abusing a ChatGPT feature and ClickFix tricks to deliver a potent trojan to users searching for ChatGPT on Google. Target: Users searching for ChatGPT via Google. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] AI-generated ClickFix sites on typosquatted domains deliver SmartRAT
item.description: In March 2026 Zscaler ThreatLabz saw typosquatting domains hosting malicious content made with AI website builders to run ClickFix lures delivering SmartRAT. Target: Users visiting typosquatted domains. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Talos IR: public-sector credential theft via phishing page vibe-coded on Softr AI builder
item.description: Cisco Talos IR's Q1 2026 report described a public-sector phishing case where the page targeting Exchange and OWA logins was built on Softr with a few AI prompts and no code, exfiltrating credentials to Google Sheets. Target: Public administration employees' Exchange and OWA accounts. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] COINBAIT crypto-exchange phishing kit built with Lovable AI app builder
item.description: GTIG found COINBAIT, a React single-page phishing kit imitating a crypto exchange, attributed to financially motivated cluster UNC5356, with Supabase and lovable.app artefacts showing Lovable AI-built code. Target: Cryptocurrency exchange customers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Scam networks in Cambodia, Myanmar and Nigeria used ChatGPT for investment-fraud personas
item.description: Organised scam operations in Cambodia, Myanmar and Nigeria used ChatGPT to translate messages, generate social-media content and build investment personas, even asking it to strip em dashes to hide AI authorship. Target: Social-media users targeted by investment and romance scams. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Microsoft blocks phishing campaign using LLM-generated obfuscated SVG files
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence detected credential phishing using SVG attachments posing as PDFs whose verbose obfuscated code was likely written by an LLM. Target: US organizations. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Proofpoint: Lovable AI builder abused for Tycoon MFA phishing hitting 5,000+ organisations
item.description: Proofpoint saw tens of thousands of malicious Lovable URLs a month since February 2025; one Tycoon campaign hit over 5,000 organisations with AI-built fake Microsoft logins capturing MFA tokens and session cookies. Target: Microsoft 365 users, UPS customers, Aave wallet holders. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Wrong Number: Cambodia task scam used ChatGPT to translate SMS lures into six languages
item.description: A centralised Cambodia-based operation generated recruitment-style messages in six languages offering pay for trivial tasks, routing responders from SMS to WhatsApp to a Telegram mentor; one lure hit an OpenAI staffer. Target: UK mobile users recruited via SMS, WhatsApp and Telegram. GB. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] VAGue Focus: China-linked accounts used ChatGPT to social-engineer US officials and press
item.description: Accounts active in mainland Chinese business hours posed as staff of Focus Lens News, BrightWave Media Europe and Visionary Advisory Group, translating social-engineering messages and polishing letters to a US senator. Target: US senator's office, journalists and researchers. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] FBI warns AI-voice vishing campaign impersonates senior US officials to hijack accounts
item.description: FBI PSA I-051525 said that since April 2025 actors have sent smishing texts and AI-generated voice messages posing as senior US officials to build rapport, push malicious links and take over accounts. Target: Senior US federal and state officials and their contacts. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Recruitment-fraud ring used Claude to polish fake hiring-manager lures in Eastern Europe
item.description: A moderately sophisticated group impersonating hiring managers at real companies had Claude rewrite non-native English into fluent messages, craft interview scripts and format lures to harvest applicants' personal data. Target: Job seekers in Eastern European countries. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] AkiraBot uses GPT-4o-mini to spam 80,000 websites through contact forms and chat widgets
item.description: SentinelLABS exposed AkiraBot, a Python framework that scrapes each target site and asks OpenAI to write unique SEO spam, bypassing CAPTCHAs; it targeted 420,000 domains and hit at least 80,000 since September 2024. Target: Small business sites on Shopify, Wix, Squarespace, GoDaddy. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Cambodia-based romance-baiting scam used ChatGPT to generate multilingual social lures
item.description: A likely Cambodia-based network translated and generated comments in Japanese, Chinese and English for romance and investment scams, which OpenAI disrupted alongside a separate Urdu-English task scam. Target: Social-media users in Japan, China and English markets. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] GhostGPT: uncensored chatbot sold on Telegram to write malware and phishing for criminals
item.description: Abnormal Security documented GhostGPT, a jailbroken LLM wrapper sold via Telegram with a no-logs claim, that produced a convincing DocuSign phishing email on request and is marketed for malware and exploit work. Target: Businesses targeted by phishing and BEC. GL. Verification: confirmed.
